text:
derek: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's tiling change (commit f2c3b9) flashv3 fused attention shows ~10-18% throughput regression on short-medium seqs.

sasha: Can you paste the bench numbers? which model/seq/batch?

derek: microbench (gpt2-medium-ish):
```
config: seq=512, batch=8, kv_cache=enabled
before: 95k tokens/sec, p50=22.4ms
after: 78k tokens/sec, p50=27.1ms
```

maria: nvprof counters from the "after" run (trimmed):
```
DRAM read BW: 182 GB/s
L1/shared mem throughput: 34 GB/s
SM active ratio: 0.68
issued_warps_stalled_mem: +22%
```

alyssa: interesting — did kvcache hit rate change? paged attention fallback could be copying pages around and hitting DRAM.

derek: good call. batch=8 shows worst regression; batch=1-2 unaffected. kvcache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 77% in these runs.

sasha: sounds like paged-attn + tiling changed the eviction pattern. Maybe our tiler increases active set per-block causing more page churn. Can you dump kvcache trace?

ci-bot: Build #3287 finished — linked: https://ci.redwood/inference/3287 — includes f2c3b9

maria: quick kvcache trace snippet (recent entries):
```
[evict] block=0x7f.. len=128 seq=256 last_used=1612
[load]  block=0x4a.. from host memcpy 16MB
[miss]  page_fetch latency ~1.2ms
```

derek: hypothesis: tiling split causes more mini-tiles per warp; fused kernel now issues more SM shared loads and increases concurrent DRAM traffic. Combined with paged-attn misses -> BW saturation.

alyssa: possible short-term mitigation: reduce paged-chunk-size to 64KB or prefer non-paged fused flash kernel when kvcache hit ratio > 85%.

sasha: PR idea: add kernel selector guard that prefers fused-flash if (kvcache_hit_rate > 0.9 && estimated_shared_mem_usage < 0.85*smem_cap && expected_seq <= 640). failing that, fall back to paged variant.

maria: ran a quick patch (reduced chunk-size + selector tweak) on staging node: throughput for batch=8 improved from 78k -> 87k tokens/sec; p50 down to 24.0ms. not full recovery but better.

derek: nice. can we also try lowering per-warp tile_work items to reduce concurrent DRAM bursts? maybe pipeline stages=2 -> 1 reduces mem spikes.

sasha: schedule: I'll open an issue with profiling artifacts, and a small follow-up PR to (1) add selector guard, (2) expose tile_work tunable and pipeline stages flag for runtime experiments.

alyssa: I can run a matrix across seq=[256,512,768] batch=[4,8,16] on dedicated node (ded-node-14) this afternoon and post raw counters + nsys traces.

derek: thanks. if alyssa's numbers look good we'll roll the selector tweak to canary and monitor BW per-GPU. @ci-bot please schedule perf job for canary.

ci-bot: scheduled perf/regression job #3290

sasha: action items: open issue, PR for selector + flags, perf matrix by alyssa, add kvcache hitrate telemetry to console for quick detection. :eyes:

maria: one more note — nvprof shows an increase in L1/shared miss rate after tiling change; could be we need a small smem_alignment tweak in kernel launcher.

derek: agreed. include smem alignment and try pipeline stages toggles in matrix. thanks all.
